body:
Priya (Support): FYI - ACME reported a production failure with JSON mode streaming. They get JSONDecodeError in py-sdk when the model returns a long string containing emojis. Happens intermittently on large responses. Request id: req_0a1b2c3d, customer env: Dedicated-us-west.

Maya K (Customer Success): Reproduced once on our side with a long chat completion > 8k tokens. Python stack: json.decoder.JSONDecodeError: Unterminated string starting at: line 1 column 5123 (char 5122). Customer sees ~10% of streams fail and app crashes.

Jamie (SDK): Which SDK versions? any proxy in front of them?

Priya (Support): py-sdk 0.9.2, ts-sdk 1.4.0, go-client 0.7.1. They use our hosted endpoint with streaming=true and mode=json_mode (they set "json": true in request). No proxy except company load balancer.

Sergio (SRE): Can you paste a raw wire capture or chunk sequence? This sounds like chunk boundary inside an escape sequence or multi-byte UTF-8 char.

Priya (Support): Paste from customer tcpdump (sanitized). The server sends NDJSON-like frames. Note how a unicode surrogate / escape is split across chunks:

Chunk 1:
{"id":1,"choices":[{"delta":{"content":"Hello \uD83D"}}

Chunk 2:
\uDE00","done":false}]}

When concatenated by some streaming parsers the split escape becomes invalid on the receiver if the SDK passes chunks through to json.loads() before stitching.

Jamie (SDK): OK that explains the JSONDecodeError in py-sdk: our streaming parser tries to decode each newline-delimited chunk immediately. If the chunk ends mid-escape ("\\uD83D"), json.loads() fails. TS and Go libraries show similar behavior in their streaming helpers.

Alex R (Eng Runtime): Do we guarantee chunk boundaries align to JSON token boundaries? The runtime is optimized for throughput and does not ensure token-aligned chunks. We rely on SDKs to reassemble frames.

Jamie (SDK): Current heuristics: bufferUntilCompleteObject: we look for trailing '\n' and attempt to parse per-line. In this case the server doesn't emit a newline between the split pieces. We should change parser to be more tolerant: incremental JSON decoder that appends until a full object can be parsed. Python has json.JSONDecoder.raw_decode that can be used incrementally.

Priya (Support): Customer wants immediate workaround. They can set streaming=false but that hurts latency/cost. Any quick SDK patch we can push?

Jamie (SDK): I'll cut a py-sdk patch to buffer partial frames and only call json.loads once an object completes. Quick patch: accumulate chunks in a bytes buffer and try incremental decode; fallback to full parse on timeout. For TS/Go I'll add similar fixes but may be slightly slower.

Sergio (SRE): Also document in guides: server may split UTF-16 escape sequences or multi-byte UTF-8 across TCP segments. SDKs should handle reassembly. We should add tests that simulate mid-escape splits.

Maya K (Customer Success): I'll tell the customer we have a patch incoming and provide the temporary workaround: disable streaming or add a short client-side retry on JSONDecodeError to rejoin remaining chunks.

deploy-bot: Deployed py-sdk patch branch: fix/streaming-incremental-parse -> staging

Jamie (SDK): Action items:
- Jamie: push py-sdk patch to prod tomorrow (unit + integration tests simulate split escapes)
- Jamie: open tickets for ts/go SDK incremental decoders
- Alex: confirm runtime will not change chunking semantics (we'll log this in docs)
- Sergio: help capture one more tcpdump from customer and provide sample to SDK team
- Priya/Maya: update customer with ETA and mitigation

Priya (Support): Marking P1 escalation. Thanks all, I'll follow up with the customer thread and link to this slack.
